answer: Cap reputation velocity like a glacier: trust accrues at a fixed daily rate, so no identity can outpace physics. As a head climbs the canyon of trust tiers, each ascent demands a fresh non-outsourceable proof; reaching the zenith forces a full-history audit, replayable by any peer from the ledger. A clone cannot speed up its own curve, share one audit across heads, or leap a tier, so every fake must pay real wall-clock days before it matters — time per head, unamortizable across a fleet.
